findings.description: os.system() call with system-controlled paths - no command injection risk
findings.reasoning: This is a false positive. The os.system() call constructs a command using sys.executable (the Python interpreter path) and f.name (a temporary file path from tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile()). Both values are controlled by the system/Python runtime, not user input. There is no way for an attacker to inject commands through this call. The CodeQL query flags all os.system() calls but this one is safe because it doesn't incorporate any untrusted data.

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".py") as f:
    print(f"downloading {URL} into {f.name}")

    req = urlopen(URL, **kwargs)
    data = req.read()
    req.close()
    f.write(data)
    f.flush()
    print("download finished, installing pip")
    code = os.system(
        f"{sys.executable} {f.name} --user --upgrade"
        " --break-system-packages"
    )
evidence.notes: sys.executable is the Python interpreter path (system-controlled) and f.name is a temporary file path created by tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile() (system-controlled). Neither value comes from user input or external untrusted sources.
